title: How much of an open-source chip design search can cheap fidelity rungs and proof prediction save, with a guarantee?
lede: research programme (proposal only): multi-fidelity, verification-aware design-space search on SKY130 place-and-route, with 12 checked references, hypotheses H1 to H5 and MLCAD as the target venue
summary: An open research programme, not a result. Open chip flows (Yosys, ABC, OpenROAD) let a laptop run RTL to routed layout, but each run is slow and a search needs hundreds, so searches trust cheap estimates whose ranking can differ from the routed one (measured on one set in chip-pnr). The programme asks how much cost multi-fidelity search (successive halving, Hyperband, BOHB, multi-fidelity Bayesian optimisation) saves across four rungs (generic gates, liberty mapping, placement, global route), whether a conformal calibration on a small routed pilot gives the shortlist a coverage guarantee whatever the bias, and whether formal-equivalence success can be predicted cheaply and charged inside the budget. Hypotheses H1 to H5 each name the result that refutes them. No experiment has been run; milestone 1 measures rung-to-rung bias on at least eight designs.
